23 A trace is shown on the screen of a cathode-ray oscilloscope (c.r.o.).
1.0 cm
1.0 cm
The time-base setting is 2.5 ms cm–1 and the Y-gain is 2.0 V cm–1.
What is the frequency and the amplitude of the waveform displayed by the c.r.o.?
amplitude
frequency
/ V
/ Hz
A
0.00375
4.0
B
0.00375
8.0
C
267
4.0
D
267
8.0

hints: Count squares on the trace: one complete sine cycle occupies $1.5\text{ cm}$ horizontally, and the peak is $2.0\text{ cm}$ above the centre line.
Recall that horizontal length x time-base $2.5\text{ ms cm}^{-1}$ gives period $T$, and vertical height x Y-gain $2.0\text{ V cm}^{-1}$ gives voltage.
Use $f = 1/T$ with $T$ in seconds for frequency, and use only centre-to-peak height, not trough-to-peak, for amplitude.
walkthrough: Read the horizontal scale: measure one full wave from peak to next peak. It spans $1.5\text{ cm}$ on the screen.
Apply the time-base: $T = 1.5\text{ cm} \times 2.5\text{ ms cm}^{-1} = 3.75\text{ ms} = 0.00375\text{ s}$.
Calculate frequency: $f = 1/T = 1/0.00375\text{ s} \approx 267\text{ Hz}$. The value $0.00375$ alone is the period, not the frequency.
Read the vertical scale: amplitude is centre-line to peak. The peak is $2.0\text{ cm}$ above the centre.
Apply the Y-gain: $V_0 = 2.0\text{ cm} \times 2.0\text{ V cm}^{-1} = 4.0\text{ V}$. Using trough-to-peak $4.0\text{ cm}$ would wrongly give $8.0\text{ V}$.
Combine $267\text{ Hz}$ and $4.0\text{ V}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Amplitude $4.0\text{ V}$ is correct for a $2.0\text{ cm}$ peak height, but $0.00375$ is the period $T$ in $\text{s}$, not $f = 1/T$.

B.explanation: The value $0.00375$ is the period in $\text{s}$ and $8.0\text{ V}$ is the peak-to-peak voltage, not the frequency and amplitude.

C.explanation: Period $T = 3.75\text{ ms}$ gives $f \approx 267\text{ Hz}$ and a $2.0\text{ cm}$ peak gives $4.0\text{ V}$ amplitude.

D.explanation: Frequency $267\text{ Hz}$ is correct, but $8.0\text{ V}$ uses the full $4.0\text{ cm}$ trough-to-peak height instead of the $2.0\text{ cm}$ centre-to-peak amplitude.
